description: Evaluation benchmarks for the interactive-html (Answer Me With Interactive HTML) skill, verifying self-contained single-file HTML generation, interactive time scrubbers, parameter sliders, live state inspectors, in-page prediction challenges, and sandbox compliance.

evals.name: btree-vs-fullscan-interactive-html
evals.prompt: answer me with interactive html: how does a database B+ Tree index find a row so much faster than a Full Table Scan?
assertions: Writes a self-contained single-file .html document inside the project workspace (e.g. .interactive-html/) and never to /tmp
Includes a step-by-step Time Scrubber (Prev, Play/Pause, Next, Reset, range input) allowing reversible traversal of the search steps
Includes at least one interactive parameter control (e.g. target key selector, dataset size slider, or B+ Tree vs Full Scan comparison toggle)
Renders an inline SVG or DOM visual stage highlighting visited tree nodes and discarded branches alongside a live read-count State Inspector
Includes an in-page interactive prediction challenge with immediate feedback
Uses zero external fetch() calls or unverified third-party CDNs

evals.name: js-event-loop-stepper-html
evals.prompt: /interactive-html explain the JavaScript event loop and why Promise.resolve().then() runs before setTimeout(fn, 0)
assertions: Generates an interactive HTML debugger showing the Call Stack, Web APIs, Microtask Queue, and Macrotask Queue
Provides a step scrubber that moves items visually between Call Stack, Microtask Queue, and Macrotask Queue tick by tick
Displays synchronized code line highlighting and live console output at each step
Supports switching between preset code snippets or toggling microtask vs macrotask scheduling
Concludes with an interactive predict-the-console-output challenge inside the HTML page

evals.name: token-bucket-rate-limiter-eli5
evals.prompt: explain how a Token Bucket API rate limiter works like I'm 10 years old, answer me with interactive html
assertions: Uses a child-friendly physical metaphor (e.g. arcade token bucket, ticket dispenser, water bucket) with zero unexplained jargon
Includes live interactive sliders for refill rate and bucket capacity plus a button to fire burst requests
Animates accepted requests versus rejected (429 / bounced) requests visually in real time
Includes a kid-friendly in-page prediction question checking what happens when a burst exceeds the bucket size

evals.name: raft-consensus-split-brain-sim
evals.prompt: build an interactive html explanation of Raft leader election and what happens during a network partition (split brain)
assertions: Renders a multi-node cluster stage showing Follower, Candidate, and Leader states with term numbers and heartbeat/vote messages
Provides an interactive fault-injection toggle or preset to partition the network into minority vs majority quorums
Shows live per-node state (currentTerm, votedFor, commitIndex) in a State Inspector panel
Explains why a minority partition cannot commit writes using an interactive challenge
